newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES -AUG 11.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business weeklies. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- The U.S. AS Corporation and Bulgaria's firm Niki Star have applied for a central bank permission to acquire stakes in the private Balkan Universal Bank (BUB), offering to buy up to 75 percent or up to 45 percent each, respectively.
Both companies have pledged to raise the bank's capital to 10 billion levs to meet new central bank minimum capital requirements. BUB sources said the bank preffered the potential Bulgarian buyer.

-- Shareholders in Sofia Municipal Bank decided to adopt a two-tier management system through supervisory and executive boards in a bid the meet stricter management requirements under Bulgaria's new banking law. Shareholders also decided to raise the bank's capital at a meeting in mid-October.

-- Shareholders in Bulgaria's largest steelworks Kremikovtzi approved a two-tier management system and decided to raise capital to 200 billion levs from 18.5 billion levs. Under a government plan 30 percent of the company's equity would be offered to investors.
-- Bulgaria is planning to set up a National Arms Company, which is to unite all Bulgarian firms dealing in production, repair and trade in arms and military equipment.
-- Trade and Tourism Minister Valentin Vasilev met executive directors of Bulgaria's holiday resorts to discuss options to speed up privatisation in tourism. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
